narrative.overview: This sidecar records shipped v2 only; v1 remains separate. V2 is a warm 2D career adventure where a centered pixel hero traverses seven geometric landmarks while paper HUD, story, and quest surfaces keep the evidence path legible. The selected stop color becomes the live accent across navigation and state.
keyCharacteristics: Fixed paper HUD framing a horizontally translated seven-stop world.
Centered CSS pixel hero with animated limbs during stage travel.
Independent far-mountain, near-mountain, world, ground, and road layers.
Active-accent landmark, beacon, story, focus, progress, and scrollbar.
Modal project and map drawers with keyboard containment and restoration.
Compact mobile project stages that preserve the project-entry action.

rules.name: The Active Stage Rule
rules.body: Use the current stop color as the single live accent across the hero, landmark, story, focus, progress, and scrollbar.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Pretendard names destinations and explains them, separated by weight and size, and IBM Plex Mono reports game state.

rules.name: The Centered Hero Rule
rules.body: Keep the character fixed and move world layers at distinct rates.

rules.name: The Modal Quest Rule
rules.body: Project proof and map routing open as focused drawers and return focus to their trigger.

rules.name: The Responsive Quest Rule
rules.body: Below 480px, project stages hide narrative and chips while retaining title, subtitle, and entry action.

dos: Do keep v2 game-first and preserve v1 separately.
Do preserve all seven stops and all four navigation modes.
Do preserve parallax depth, active-stage color continuity, and project evidence.
Do trap dialog focus, close on Escape, restore focus, and inert the background.
Do honor reduced motion and preserve the compact mobile project CTA.
donts: Don't restore the stale control-room evidence-ledger design or inline tabs.
Don't flatten the independent parallax layers.
Don't add project entry actions to non-project stages.
Don't fire movement shortcuts from controls or while a drawer is open.
Don't remove stage colors, phrase-safe Korean, or mobile prioritization.
